counterfactual_missing_items: No epistaxis or nasopharyngeal origin to support juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
No ground-glass osseous matrix to support fibrous dysplasia
No granulomatous inflammation, vasculitis, or systemic organ involvement to support granulomatosis with polyangiitis
decisive_items: Tissue analysis showed spindle cell process in a patternless arrangement with significant multinucleated giant cells
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells.
Left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved.
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete: it retains R2's diagnostic histology (spindle cells with multinucleated giant cells, no atypia) and adds the bone-anatomy spans (maxillary/ethmoid erosion, alveolar ridge involvement, remodeling), specifying giant cell tumor of bone. R2 lacks this anatomic completion. R3 is disfavored by female sex and non-angiofibroma histology; R1 lacks giant-cell histology and ground-glass imaging; R4 lacks vasculitic/granulomatous histology and systemic features.

rejected.why: Teenage girl and biopsy showing spindle/giant cells rather than vascular fibrous stroma; no epistaxis or nasopharyngeal origin.
Biopsy shows multinucleated giant cells, not fibrous-osseous trabeculae; imaging shows a solid/cystic mass rather than ground-glass bony change.
No granulomatous inflammation, necrosis, vasculitis, or pulmonary/renal involvement; histology is a spindle-cell giant-cell process.
